This is formal. Let 
<MATH_0001>
be a diagram as in Definition <REF_0001>. We have to show that
<MATH_0002>
is an equivalence. Using the definition of the <MATH_0003>-fibre product
this becomes
<MATH_0004>
We are given that each of the functors
<MATH_0005>
are equivalences. An object of the right hand side of
(<REF_0002>) is a system
<MATH_0006>
Then <MATH_0007> is isomorphic to the image of an object
<MATH_0008> in <MATH_0009> and <MATH_0010> is isomorphic
to the image of an object <MATH_0011> of <MATH_0012>. The pair of
morphisms <MATH_0013> corresponds to a morphism <MATH_0014>
between the images of <MATH_0015> and <MATH_0016> in <MATH_0017>.
Then <MATH_0018> is an object of the left hand side of
(<REF_0003>) mapping to the given object of the
right hand side. This proves that (<REF_0004>) is
essentially surjective. We omit the proof that it is fully faithful.
